C001.reason: The schema change widens speed_mps from float32 to float64 (float to double). The generated C# property SpeedMps will now be double. The explicit cast (float)request.Speed narrows the double input to float32, which contradicts the intended behavior of preserving input precision through serialization. Remove the cast so the double value flows directly into the double property.

C002.reason: entity.SpeedMps is read into a Dictionary<string, object>. After the schema change, the generated property type becomes double, which is assignment-compatible with object. The observation key "speed_mps" and the value semantics remain unchanged. No source edit is required.

C003.reason: The comparison entity.SpeedMps > 30.0 uses a double literal (30.0). After the schema change, entity.SpeedMps becomes double, so the comparison remains a double > double operation with identical semantics. The constructed_payload uses the sample built in C001, which will now serialize a double field. No source edit is required here.

rationale: The schema change widens wire field 2 from float to double. The generated C# property SpeedMps changes from float to double. The only necessary runtime change is to stop narrowing the double input (request.Speed) to float when constructing the outbound message. All reads and observations (dictionary value, threshold comparison) are already compatible with double and require no edits. The wire encoding will now use double precision, matching the new schema.
assumptions: Protobuf code generation maps proto3 double to C# double and float to float.
The coordinated rollout ensures all consumers expect double on wire field 2.
JsonSerializer.Deserialize reads JSON numbers into double for the TelemetryRequest.Speed property.
Dictionary<string, object> accepts double values without boxing changes.
The > operator on double preserves the strict >30.0 threshold semantics.
